Tang criterion as quoted in Harkin 2023 Eq. 5, primary not in the library; sourced for measured melt pool geometry; with analytic geometry Harkin 2023 Eq. 9 to 11 and Conclusions find the unit value problematic (Ti-6Al-4V, one machine); here applied to modelled geometry, a screening, not a prediction. At dH/hs >= 15 the transition and keyhole depth is biased low because the keyhole absorptance A(R) is not modelled, so a lack-of-fusion fail in this regime may be a model artefact.

Keyhole mode by the served regime classifier: ΔH/hₛ = 20.89 at or above the cut 20 (Keyhole Mode (melt-pool D/W > 0.5 screening onset)). A regime label, not a porosity claim: keyhole mode onset, not a porosity boundary: King 2014 Conclusion (4) and Sec. 5.6 (30 +/- 4 for 316L, 50 um powder layer) with Conclusions (1) and (5) (voids appear in keyhole mode and increase far above the threshold, a qualitative association); Cunningham 2019 p.2 (keyhole threshold and morphology by x-ray imaging); Zhao 2020 (Science 370, 1080: energy density threshold about 3.7 MJ/m2 below which no keyhole pores form, no pore condition below index 15, stable keyholes up to 62); Huang 2022 (doi 10.1038/s41467-022-28694-x: the transition to unstable keyhole melting is alloy dependent, H/hm x Lth about 8 +/- 3 for Ti-6Al-4V and 20 +/- 3 for Al7A77 in that paper's units); cut 20: transferred from the 316L and Ti-6Al-4V bases, not derived for this alloy.

Advisory: P–v is outside the in718 literature display range (120–300 W, 550–1000 mm/s): unsourced screening threshold: P-v display range, no table or figure for any edge; windows depend on spot size and layer thickness (Hofmann 2026 Fig. 5, PDF p.5); a single track window does not ensure bulk printing (Vaglio and Totis 2020). It does not change the verdict.
